paragraphs: R. Matnia or Matnaya. (Matanya is King Zedekiah, II Kings 24:17.) His father's name was R. Yudan, who is mentioned many times as R. Yudan, father of R. Matnaya, as in Demai ch. 7 halakha 4; see his entry. The son, R. Matnia [the entry’s subject], was, in Hyman’s assessment, a leading figure of his generation among the Amoraim of Eretz Israel, in the 4th-5th generation. He is mentioned in the Yerushalmi, Beitzah ch. 5 halakha 2-19,

R. Abba Mari and R. Matnaya were sitting; they saw a man dividing water this way and that and drinking. R. Abba Mari said to R. Matniah: This is what R. Yaakov bar Zavdi [ב״ז] said. And in Beitzah ch. 1, end of halakha 7: R. Liezer and R. Abba Mari and R. Matnia issued a ruling concerning bread for Ursicinus [ארסקינס] on the Sabbath, etc. Hyman identifies this R. Liezer as ר״א (R. Eliezer or R. Elazar; abbreviation left unexpanded) son of R. Yose the latter.

And in Shabbat ch. 7 halakha 2-26 he disputes with R. Acha bar Rav. And there, ch. 12 halakha 4, he disputes with R. Yudan son of R. Shalom. And in Sheviit ch. 8 halakha 1 he disputes R. Bun bar Chiyya. And we find in Yevamot ch. 7 end of halakha 5: R. Matnaya said, I went up to trade and heard R. Yochanan and R.

Yishmael sons of Yishua; and Hyman asserts an error, with the supplied abbreviation בל״ם unresolved, in these names. And in Gittin ch. 5 halakha 3: R. Shmuel son of R. Yose son of R. Bun and R. Matnia were sitting, thinking to say; R. Yose son of R. Bun said to them, etc. Hyman infers from this that he lived long, for R. Shmuel was among the last Amoraim mentioned in the Yerushalmi.

Hyman concludes from the personal details that he was a merchant, as cited above. And in Ketubot, beginning of ch. 1, that he changed an ancient custom, whereby they would betroth twelve months before the bride entered the chuppah, but he arranged for his daughter the betrothal and the chuppah together.

notes.text: The source prints בל״ם, not the registry-listed בל״ס; rendered literally as printed, with the apparent sense 'without doubt' tentatively adopted, no expansion supplied.

Printed 'ב״ז' after R. Yaakov is an unresolved abbreviation (possibly ben/bar plus a name); kept literal. 'ארסקינס' kept as 'Arsakenes', a tentative transliteration. Chapter/halakha numbers are Hyman's printed locators, not converted to modern numbering.

Printed 'אמרי' etc. Locators like ה״ב-יט, ה״ב-כו are preserved as printed and unresolved; 'ר״א בר׳ יוסי האחרון' rendered as R. Eliezer son of R. Yose the latter, preserving Hyman's identification as his assertion.

The complete named Beitzah paragraphs support Yaakov bar Zavdi and the Ursicinus comparison; the bring/bake alternatives occur in the edition’s commentary and do not require a more specific translation of Hyman’s הורי פיתא. The supplied בל״ם does not become בל״ס or “without doubt” merely because an earlier model suggested it. Historical notes and the root’s qualifications remain in full.

The consulted Demai 7:4 expressly calls Rabbi Yudan Matnaya’s father. Beitzah 5:2 and 1:7 support Yaakov bar Zavdi and Ursicinus; the bring/bake alternatives belong to the cited edition’s commentary, so Hyman’s bread ruling remains neutral. Shabbat 7:2, 12:4 and Sheviit 8:1 support the named disputants. The corresponding Yevamot passage is at 7:6:2 in the consulted Guggenheimer text, which also has Yochanan and Yishmael sons of Yeshua; Hyman’s supplied locator, proposed name corruption and unresolved בל״ם remain his report. Gittin 5:3 explicitly has Yose son of Bun speaking to both seated scholars, supporting “said to them” for Hyman’s abbreviation א״ל. Hyman’s longevity, generation, merchant and marriage-custom arguments remain attributed, without new identity or chronology admission. The two source holds remain in force.

Hyman's printed notice (vol. III, p. 917) appears to read בל״ס, ordinarily ‘without doubt,’ where the supplied Hebrew reads בל״ם. The consulted Yerushalmi Yevamot 7:6:2 names Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yishmael, sons of Yeshua, in Matnaya's account of a trading trip. Hyman's supplied locator and his assertion of an error in those names are retained.

The consulted Ketubot 1:1 says that Rabbi Matnaya did this for his daughter in the discussion of betrothal at the chuppah. The surrounding passage discusses court days and the interval before a claim could be heard. The former custom of a twelve-month interval and the account of changing it are Hyman's explanation. In Gittin 5:3, Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Bun addresses the two seated scholars. The longevity and generational conclusions are Hyman's deductions.
